problem: Find the asymptotes of the hyperbola $9{x}^{2}-16{y}^{2}=144.$
worked_solution:
The standard equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin is

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

For a horizontal hyperbola centered at the origin, the equations of the asymptotes are

$$
y=\pm \frac{b}{a}x.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, we divide both sides of the equation by $144$ and then simplify, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}9{x}^{2}-16{y}^{2} & =144 \\ \frac{9{x}^{2}}{144}-\frac{16{y}^{2}}{144} & =\frac{144}{144} \\ \frac{{x}^{2}}{16}-\frac{{y}^{2}}{9} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have $a=\sqrt{16}=4,$ and $b=\sqrt{9}=3.$ 

Therefore, the asymptotes are $y=\pm \frac{3}{4}x.$
